prompt.context_jp: 崩れかけた瓦礫の隙間から白い煙＿＿上がり、遠くでサイレンが鳴り響いていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for introducing the smoke rising from the rubble?

feedback.correct_en: The opening sentence introduces the smoke as new, perceived information in the disaster scene — が marks this fresh, 'camera-pan' detail.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat the smoke as an already-established topic, which is wrong for the very first sentence. を doesn't fit the intransitive 上がる.

prompt.context_jp: 医師の姿＿＿まだ、どこにも見えなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 医師の姿＿＿まだ…見えなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the contrastive 'as for the doctor…'?

feedback.correct_en: After introducing smoke, victims, and sirens, this line pivots: 'the doctor, however, was nowhere to be seen.' は highlights that contrast with everything that WAS present.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would read as neutral new information, losing the pointed 'but no doctor' feel. に marks a location/target, not the subject here.

contrast_examples.jp: 声は聞こえたが、姿は見えなかった。
contrast_examples.en: The voice was heard, but the figure wasn't seen.

prompt.context_jp: 新しい医療組織の綱領＿＿まさに読み上げられようとしている、その大事な朝である。
prompt.prompt_jp: 綱領＿＿読み上げられようとしている…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the charter inside this descriptive relative clause?

feedback.correct_en: Inside a relative/adnominal clause modifying 朝, the embedded subject must take が, not は. は is reserved for the main-clause topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: は can't appear in this kind of embedded modifier here. を would require a transitive active verb, but 読み上げられる is passive.

contrast_examples.en: The ceremony starts in the morning. (main clause topic)

prompt.context_jp: 壇上の赤塚知事＿＿、迷いのない声で新組織の理念を語り続けた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for the governor as the established topic of this paragraph?

feedback.correct_en: The governor has already been set up at the podium; the sentence tells us what she goes on doing. は marks her as the running topic, carrying the narrative forward.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would reintroduce her as new information, which clashes with the already-established scene. で would mark a location/means.

contrast_examples.jp: 赤塚知事は語り続けた。
そこへ赤塚知事が現れた。

prompt.context_jp: 肝心の音羽の姿＿＿どこにもなく、名前だけが宙に浮いていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 音羽の姿＿＿どこにもなく…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits here, where Otoha is contrasted with the others who did show up?

feedback.correct_en: The other members have already assembled; this line singles Otoha out as the exception. は picks him out contrastively against the gathered team.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just report his absence as fresh info, losing the 'but Otoha, of all people…' flavor. も would mean 'also,' which contradicts 'nowhere.'

contrast_examples.jp: 冬木はいるが、音羽の姿はない。
contrast_examples.en: Fuyuki is here, but Otoha is nowhere to be seen.

contrast_examples.jp: 急に音羽の姿が現れた。

prompt.context_jp: 肝心の音羽の姿はどこにもなく、名前だけ＿＿宙に浮いていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 名前だけ＿＿宙に浮いていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle pairs naturally with だけ to say 'only his name was floating'?

feedback.correct_en: 〜だけが gives the exhaustive 'only X, nothing else' reading needed here: his body is absent, only his name remains.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would mean 'at least his name' (with other things possibly also), weakening the exclusivity. に marks a location, not the subject.

contrast_examples.jp: 名前だけは覚えている。
contrast_examples.en: At least the name, I remember.

prompt.context_jp: チームとしての体裁＿＿まだ整っていないことは、誰の目にも明らかだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 体裁＿＿まだ整っていないこと…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the embedded clause modifying こと?

feedback.correct_en: This は-marked topic ('that the team wasn't ready') contains an embedded subject. Inside こと-clauses, subjects normally take が, not は.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside こと here would create a double-は with the outer 'ことは,' which is awkward. を would require a transitive verb.

contrast_examples.jp: 準備が整っていないことは明らかだ。

prompt.context_jp: 理念が言葉であるうちはよかったが、いま試されるの＿＿現場での実力そのものである。
prompt.prompt_jp: 試されるの＿＿現場での実力そのものである。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the cleft 'what is being tested is…'?

feedback.correct_en: This is a 〜のは〜だ cleft contrasting 'words/ideals' with 'real on-site skill.' は is the fixed topic marker in this structure, highlighting what's really at stake now.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would break the cleft and lose the contrastive framing. を doesn't fit — 試される is passive.

contrast_examples.en: Ability is being tested (plain, not cleft).

prompt.context_jp: 初出動というだけでも足がすくむのに、頼るべきチーフ＿＿正体不明の男である。
prompt.prompt_jp: 頼るべきチーフ＿＿正体不明の男である。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits for the chief Hina ought to rely on?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence frames the chief as the topic and then says what he is ('an unknown man'). は fits the 'as for the chief she should rely on…' structure, and adds a wry contrastive edge.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce the chief as new information, which clashes — he's already been set up in the scene. で would need a different predicate.

contrast_examples.en: The person I should rely on is absent.

contrast_examples.jp: そこへ頼れる人が現れた。

prompt.context_jp: 千住の怒声を背に受けながらも、喜多見の足＿＿止まらなかった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 喜多見の足＿＿止まらなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle best captures the 'even so, his feet didn't stop' contrast?

feedback.correct_en: The 〜ながらも setup demands a contrast: despite Senju's shouting, HIS feet didn't stop. は picks out that contrast cleanly.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would read as neutral new info and lose the 'despite that' punch. も (also) doesn't match — nothing else is 'also not stopping' here.

contrast_examples.jp: 怒鳴られても、足は止まらなかった。
contrast_examples.en: Even yelled at, his feet didn't stop.

prompt.context_jp: 時間だけ＿＿冷酷に過ぎていく。
prompt.prompt_jp: 時間だけ＿＿冷酷に過ぎていく。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle gives the 'only time, nothing else' feeling as Mei's heart stops?

feedback.correct_en: だけが pins the exhaustive 'only time' — nothing else is moving/helping, just the clock. The が underscores the stark isolation of time's passage.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは would suggest 'at least time' and lose the exclusive, cruel feeling. を doesn't fit the intransitive 過ぎる.

contrast_examples.jp: 時間だけが過ぎていった。
時間だけは守ってください。
contrast_examples.en: At least keep to the time.

prompt.context_jp: ふいにモニターの音＿＿変わった。
prompt.prompt_jp: モニターの音＿＿変わった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits the sudden change in the monitor's tone?

feedback.correct_en: ふいに ('suddenly') signals a brand-new, perceived event. が marks that fresh observation — the moment the beep changes.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn 'the monitor sound' into an already-established topic, killing the surprise. で marks location/means.

contrast_examples.jp: この音はいつもと違う。
contrast_examples.en: This sound (as a topic) is different from usual.

prompt.context_jp: しかし喜多見の指先に＿＿躊躇がなく、その動きは長い経験の積み重ねを感じさせた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 喜多見の指先に＿＿躊躇がなく…
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits after 指先に, contrasting with Hina's hesitation above?

feedback.correct_en: The previous lines show Hina frozen with doubt. 'In Kitami's fingertips, however…' takes に+は to flag that contrast of locations/people.
feedback.incorrect_en: が cannot replace this には — に marks the location of existence, and は adds the contrastive 'as for his fingertips.' を doesn't fit at all.

contrast_examples.jp: 私には迷いがある。彼には迷いがない。
contrast_examples.en: I have doubts; he has none.

prompt.context_jp: 「出血＿＿止まった」
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits this urgent in-surgery announcement?

feedback.correct_en: In the OR, a surgeon reports a fresh, observable event. が delivers that spot-news 'the bleeding stopped' with no prior framing.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply contrast with other bleeding, which isn't the point in this moment of relief. を doesn't fit intransitive 止まる.

contrast_examples.jp: 出血は止まったが、血圧がまだ低い。
contrast_examples.en: The bleeding stopped, but BP is still low. (contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 少女の呼吸＿＿浅く、意識は靄がかかったように遠ざかりつつあった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits in this descriptive report of Mei's condition?

feedback.correct_en: The sentence lines up two parallel observations about Mei (breathing / consciousness). は on each subject gives the balanced, descriptive 'as for her breathing… as for her consciousness…' rhythm.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the breathing sound like a brand-new discovery, breaking the parallel listing with 意識は. も would mean 'also,' which doesn't fit the opening of the parallel.

contrast_examples.en: Breathing is shallow; pulse is fast. (parallel description)

prompt.context_jp: 喜多見はジャケット＿＿脱ぎ捨て、ＥＲカーの後部へ跳び乗った。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle marks the jacket being thrown off?

feedback.correct_en: 脱ぎ捨てる is transitive — the jacket is the direct object getting flung aside. を marks the thing acted upon.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark it as a subject, which doesn't fit a volitional action. に would mark a destination/target.

prompt.context_jp: 駒場は現場からの映像＿＿目を凝らし、部下の動きを慎重に確認していた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which particle fits 'to strain one's eyes AT the footage'?

feedback.correct_en: 目を凝らす takes に for the target you fix your gaze on. The direct object 目 is already marked by を inside the idiom.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would create a double-を with 目を. で would read as the means/location of staring, not the target.

contrast_examples.en: Fix one's eyes on the screen.

prompt.context_jp: 「いきなり こんなところに 研修に回されるなんて ＿＿＿＿ね 比奈先生」
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrase means 'you're a lucky one' in this teasing remark?

feedback.correct_en: 持ってる (lit. 'you've got it') is a slangy set phrase meaning 'you're lucky / you've got the magic touch.' Hina's reply 持ってなんかないですよ confirms it.
feedback.incorrect_en: 持ちます is plain 'will hold/carry,' and 持たれます is a passive/polite 'be held' — neither carries the luck idiom.

contrast_examples.en: You've really got luck on your side.

prompt.context_jp: 「死者ゼロとは大きく出たね ＿＿＿＿＿といこうか」
prompt.prompt_en: Which set phrase means 'let's see what they can do'?

feedback.correct_en: お手並み拝見 ('a look at your skills') is a stock expression used, often with a slight edge, to say 'let's see what you've got.' It fits Kugayama's cool, skeptical mood.
feedback.incorrect_en: お手伝い (help) and お疲れ (tiredness) don't combine with 拝見 as set phrases — they're not idioms a politician would utter.

contrast_examples.jp: お手並み拝見といこう。
contrast_examples.en: Let's see what you can do.

prompt.context_jp: 喜多見は瞬時に頭の中で時間と処置とを＿＿＿にかけた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 時間と処置とを＿＿＿にかけた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes the idiom 'to weigh X and Y'?

feedback.correct_en: 天秤にかける ('put on a scale') is the fixed idiom for weighing two options against each other — exactly what Kitami is doing between time and procedure.
feedback.incorrect_en: 電話にかける and 手にかける exist as separate expressions ('make a call,' 'take a life/do by hand') but don't mean 'to weigh options.'

contrast_examples.jp: 命と時間を天秤にかける。

prompt.context_jp: 父親の顔から＿＿＿が引いていく。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes 'the color drained from his face'?

feedback.correct_en: 顔から血の気が引く is the standard way to describe someone going pale from shock — perfectly matching the father's horror.
feedback.incorrect_en: 空気 and 水 don't collocate with 顔から〜引く to describe fear or paling.

contrast_examples.jp: 血の気が引く思いだった。
contrast_examples.en: I felt the blood drain from me.

prompt.context_jp: その現実を補うために＿＿＿＿＿のが、この走る救命救急室なのだと知事は語った。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits 'was established/launched'?

feedback.correct_en: 立ち上げる means to launch/start up an organization or project; passive 立ち上げられた fits 'was established to complement that reality.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 立ち止まる = come to a stop; 立ち向かう = confront. Neither means 'launched.'

contrast_examples.jp: プロジェクトを立ち上げる。

prompt.context_jp: 肝臓の裂創を＿＿＿＿＿喜多見の指先は、驚くほど正確だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb fits 'having located the laceration (by feel)'?

feedback.correct_en: 探り当てる = to find by feeling/probing — perfect for Kitami's fingers locating the liver tear during surgery.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見過ごす = overlook (opposite); 打ち明ける = confess/reveal (secrets), not search.

prompt.context_jp: 近隣の救命センターとの連絡が＿＿＿＿＿に進み、受け入れ先の枠が次々と確保されていく。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word means 'rapid-fire, one after another'?

feedback.correct_en: 矢継ぎ早 (literally 'arrows loosed in quick succession') means 'in rapid succession' — fitting the dispatch center firing off hospital contacts.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手遅れ = too late; 行き当たりばったり = haphazard. Neither matches the sense of fast, efficient progress.

contrast_examples.jp: 質問を矢継ぎ早に浴びせる。
contrast_examples.en: Fire off questions in rapid succession.

prompt.context_jp: 誰もが＿＿＿の声を求めて、ようやく現れた白衣の男を見上げた。
prompt.prompt_en: Which word fits 'a voice of salvation' from the passengers' perspective?

feedback.correct_en: 救いの声 ('voice of salvation / rescue') fits the trapped passengers' desperate hope as the doctor finally arrives.
feedback.incorrect_en: 慰めの声 (words of comfort) is too mild for a disaster; 疑いの声 (voice of doubt) contradicts the moment of hope.

contrast_examples.jp: 救いの手を差し伸べる。

prompt.context_jp: Hina opens the waiting-room door and is stunned by what she sees.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural as narrative Japanese?

choices.text: 控え室の扉を押し開けた比奈は、そこに広がる光景に思わず言葉を失った。
比奈は控え室の扉を押し開けて、光景がそこに広がって、言葉を思わず失った。
控え室の扉が押し開けて、比奈はそこに光景が広がるのを言葉を失わせた。

feedback.correct_en: Option A uses a tight relative-clause structure (扉を押し開けた比奈は…) and the natural collocation 言葉を失う ('be at a loss for words'), typical of narrative prose.
feedback.incorrect_en: B strings events with て choppily and misplaces 思わず. C mangles transitivity (扉が押し開けて) and introduces a non-existent causative pattern.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼女はその光景に言葉を失った。
contrast_examples.en: She was speechless at the sight.

contrast_examples.jp: ドアを開けた彼は立ち尽くした。
contrast_examples.en: He, having opened the door, stood frozen.

prompt.context_jp: Senju, the rescue chief, is barking at Kitami to get back.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural coming from a gruff rescue team leader on-scene?

choices.text: 医者は安全なオペ室で待ってろ。危険な現場から人を救うのは俺たちの仕事だ。
お医者様におかれましては、安全な手術室でお待ちくださいませ。
医者さんは、オペ室で、ちょっと、待っていてほしいかなって思う。

feedback.correct_en: A matches Senju's blunt, male on-site register — plain imperative 待ってろ and 俺たち fit a firefighter yelling in a disaster zone.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is extreme keigo that would never come out of a rescue chief mid-rescue. C is hesitant, soft spoken-Japanese that clashes with the urgency and his character.

contrast_examples.jp: お下がりくださいませ。

prompt.context_jp: Kitami calls out to the terrified bus passengers.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural for a doctor reassuring victims?

choices.text: 皆さん！ 医師の喜多見です。もう大丈夫ですから、安心してください！
皆さんよ！ 医者の喜多見だよ。もう平気だから、落ち着けって！
皆さん！ 医師である喜多見です。既に大丈夫でございますから、ご安心あられよ。

feedback.correct_en: A hits the right calm, professional register — polite です/ます with warm 安心してください, exactly how a doctor would reassure strangers in crisis.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is too casual/pushy (落ち着けって) for a stranger in shock. C mixes stiff archaic forms (あられよ) that no modern doctor would use.

prompt.context_jp: The two doctors silently complement each other's skills in the tight space.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is the most natural narrative Japanese?

choices.text: 彼らは互いの技を無言のうちに補い合っていた。
彼らは無言のうちで互いの技術を補足し合うしていた。
彼らが無言で技をお互いにを補いあう。

feedback.correct_en: A uses the natural adverbial 無言のうちに ('wordlessly / without a word'), the idiomatic 技を補い合う, and smooth past-progressive narration.
feedback.incorrect_en: B invents 補足し合うしていた (ungrammatical double し) and misuses うちで. C has a stray を after お互いに and a tense mismatch.

contrast_examples.jp: 二人は無言のうちに頷き合った。
contrast_examples.en: The two nodded to each other without a word.

contrast_examples.jp: 弱点を補い合うチーム。
contrast_examples.en: A team that covers each other's weaknesses.

prompt.context_jp: Otowa pointedly declines Kitami's handshake.
prompt.prompt_en: Which refusal matches Otowa's cold, bureaucratic tone?

choices.text: 不必要な接触は避けましょう。
触んないでくれる？ マジで無理なんだけど。
お触りはご遠慮申し上げたく存じ上げます。

feedback.correct_en: A is clipped, impersonal, and professional — exactly how a government medical officer brushes off a handshake without being rude on the surface.
feedback.incorrect_en: B is slangy and openly hostile, wrong for a composed bureaucrat. C is over-humble keigo gone comically wrong (お触り is awkwardly intimate; 存じ上げる is misused).

contrast_examples.jp: 不要な外出は控えましょう。
